newsitem.title: DUBAI: Saudi dissident Bin Laden moved to Kandahar - paper.
newsitem.headline: Saudi dissident Bin Laden moved to Kandahar - paper.

text.p: Exiled Saudi Arabian dissident Osama bin Laden has left Afghanistan's eastern city of Jalalabad, where he had been living, for the southern city of Kandahar, a Saudi-owned newspaper reported on Tuesday.

The London-based al-Hayat quoted informed Afghan sources as saying Bin Laden, seen by Washington as one of the world's most significant sponsors of Islamic radicals, arrived in Kandahar on Friday after travelling by road with his family from Jalalabad.
The sources said the Islamic Taleban movement, which controls more than two-thirds of Afghanistan, "advised Bin Laden to move to live in Kandahar due to concern over his personal security".
They said Bin Laden was now living in a Kandahar house under Taleban protection. Both cities are controlled by Taleban and the sources did not say why Kandahar should be safer than Jalalabad.

The private Pakistan-based Afghan Islamic Press (AIP) had on Saturday quoted sources in Jalalabad as saying that Taleban flew Bin Laden and his supporters on Thursday to an unknown area, probably still in Afghanistan.
AIP said Bin Laden had been told by the Taleban not to give press interviews or issue statements against Saudi Arabia.

Bin Laden, who has denied involvement in two bombings in Saudi Arabia that killed 24 U.S. servicemen and two Indians in 1995 and 1996, has lived in Afghanistan after he was forced to leave Sudan under Saudi pressure last year.
Bin Laden, a multi-millionaire financier stripped of his Saudi citizenship, has threatened to wage a holy war on U.S. forces in the kingdom, home to Islam's two holiest shrines.
The Taleban says it will not allow the war-shattered country to be used for activities against any other nation.
